newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds follow U.S. down to close softer.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds follow U.S. down to close softer.

text.p: Canadian bonds followed a softer U.S. market to end lower in lackluster trading on Wednesday, amid little news to spur investors.

"Now we're in that kind of cusp between the election and employment numbers on Friday," said Toronto-Dominion Securities fixed-income analyst Richard Wylie. "We're in that void where trading has been pretty thin and nothing much is going on."
Wylie said Canadian bond investors followed U.S. markets lower.
Canada's 30-year benchmark slipped C$0.13 to C$112.24, yielding 7.017 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond dipped 5/32 to yield 6.88 percent. The spread between the bonds widened slightly to 14 basis points from 13 basis points at Tuesday's close.
On Friday, Canada will release May's jobless rate and the United States will report May non-farm payrolls and the unemployment rate.

Trading on Wednesday was dull except for a hiccup around the poorly bid real return bond auction, said Hank Cunningham, fixed income director at First Marathon Securities. Technical Data analyst Jeoff Hall said that "the low point of the day was the miserable re-opening of the real return bond."
"The finance department overestimated investor appetite for these inflation indexed bonds. Point of fact, there is no inflation threat in Canada," Hall wrote in a market report.
"With consumer price growth running at less than two percent per year, it is unreasonable to expect investors to pay a premium to hedge against phantom inflation."

In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond dropped C$0.18 to C$105.57 to yield 6.506 percent, while the U.S. 10-year slipped 2/32 to 6.62 percent. The negative spread between the two narrowed to 11 basis points from 13 at Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.91 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.07 percent.
